args: In libredwg/src/decode_r11.c decode_preR13 and libredwg/src/dec_macros.h UNKNOWN_UNTIL, what is the narrowest robust fix for the reported oversized dat->byte passed to bit_calc_CRC? Should decode_preR13 merely reject dat->byte > dat->size before the CRC, or is it safe and desirable for UNKNOWN_UNTIL to return DWG_ERR_VALUEOUTOFBOUNDS when pos exceeds dat->size? Please account for all contexts where UNKNOWN_UNTIL expands and whether those functions can return this error.

The ASan PoV uses an AC1009 R11 file whose attacker-controlled numheader_vars reaches UNKNOWN_UNTIL(0x6a9) in libredwg/src/header_variables_r11.spec. bit_read_TF rejects the oversized skip, but UNKNOWN_UNTIL then unconditionally sets dat->byte to the requested position. decode_preR13 in libredwg/src/decode_r11.c receives dat->byte 0x6bd with a shorter allocation and calls bit_calc_CRC over dat->byte bytes. I have confirmed there is currently no bounds check between decode_preR13_header_variables and bit_calc_CRC. I am considering a targeted validation there, potentially coupled with hardening UNKNOWN_UNTIL, but want to preserve behavior and avoid a macro change incompatible with other expansion contexts.
